"Independent cross-check task for SoringP1 #301. Do NOT edit the repository, Lean files, or the board. Scratch only under /tmp. A candidate generator for finite \"cores\" (posets with no element comparable to every other element) with e(P) <= E produced 1,053 cores for E=33 and 4,829 for E=54, where e(P) = number of linear extensions. I need an independent enumeration that does not reuse that generator's code path, to detect missing or spurious core classes.

The candidate generator starts from the 2-antichain and builds upward: (i) insert a new maximal element above any PROPER ideal of an existing core, keeping only cores; (ii) form ordinal sums A(+)B (all of A below all of B) of two existing cores; levels run n = 2..E, pruning e > E, and dedupe by one canonical-labelling function.

Your task: write your own generator using the DUAL recursion instead: start from the 2-antichain; build downward/upward with (i') inserting a new MINIMAL element below any proper filter of an existing core; (ii') ordinal sums. Justify the dual recursion from the fact that the dual order of a core is a core, of an ordinal sum A(+)B is B^d(+)A^d, and maximal elements of P correspond to minimal elements of P^d (state whether the completeness lemma used for the primal recursion transfers by duality, and where it does not). Use your OWN canonical form (e.g. brute-force canonicalization over all n! relabellings for n <= 9, and a deterministic invariant-based canonical form with collision checks for larger n) rather than the project's core_sets.canonical.

Deliver, with exact hashes of your scripts and full timing/memory:
1. Your core counts by n and total for E=12, E=20, E=33, and E=54. Known external totals from an independent full poset census are 63 at E=12 and 250 at E=20; your numbers must match those or you must explain the discrepancy.
2. A set comparison at E=33: is your set of core isomorphism classes exactly the candidate's 1,053 classes, or do you find extra/missing classes? Report any difference with explicit relation matrices and e values. The candidate set is reproducible on this machine by importing /tmp/opencode/core_only.py (read it only as the comparison target, not as a method to copy) and calling enumerate_cores(33).
3. An exhaustive independent check for n <= 8 (all posets up to isomorphism, then filter cores with e <= 33) that your set and the candidate set agree with the true answer there.
4. An explicit statement of what your cross-check does NOT establish.
Report exact counts and any discrepancy; a found missing core with e <= 33 is the most valuable possible outcome. Keep the final report under 900 words.
"
